title: Retry succeeds on the second attempt and prints a traceback anyway (exit 0)
notes:
**Fixed.** A retry that is taken now prints one located line and nothing else: `prog.pdl:1:1 - retrying after ValueError: transient failure (attempt 1 of 2)`. Exit code, stdout and the retry semantics are untouched -- the program still exits 0 and still prints `ok on attempt 2`.

The defect was three defects. (1) `process_advance_block_retry` called `traceback.format_exc()` inside its `if do_retry:` branch -- the branch PDL takes when it has *already decided the error is recoverable* -- and reported the recovery with more machinery than any real error in the catalogue. (2) The banner was wrapped in a hardcoded `\033[0;31m` ... `\033[0m` whether or not stderr was a tty, so piping to a file or a CI log embedded the escapes; the golden carried them raw, which is what made it evidence. (3) `[Retry 1/1]` reads as a failure count when it means `attempt 1 of 2 failed, retrying`, and `An error occurred in a PDL block. Error details:` narrates a crash.

The fix is a split, not a truncation. The detailed string -- traceback included -- is what `trace_error_on_retry` feeds into `pdl_context`, i.e. into the *model's* conversation for the next attempt, and `set_error_to_scope_for_retry` compares it byte for byte against the previous one to collapse a repeat, so its exact contents participate in control flow. That string is unchanged; only what is printed for the human is new. `tests/test_retry.py::test_trace_error_on_retry_keeps_the_full_error_in_the_context` pins both halves, because nothing else in the suite reads the injected message and the regression would otherwise be invisible. Colour now goes through `pdl_scheduler.colored_if_tty`, which asks the stream being written to rather than `sys.stdout` as termcolor does, and leaves `NO_COLOR` in force. The leading and trailing blank lines are gone: the fatal path prints its diagnostic unpadded and this one now matches.

Scoring. Hygiene 0 -> 3: no traceback, no ANSI on a non-tty, one well-formed line, stable across runs, exit code correct. Location stays **1** for the reason recorded before the fix and unchanged by it: `prog.pdl:1:1` is where the block starts, while the statement that raised is `code:4`, file line 7, inside a multi-line scalar -- the same coarseness that holds `E-CODE-001` at 1. The block path is absent because the retrying block is the whole program and its path is `[]`; a retry inside a nested block gets an `  in <path>` line from `located_message`, as `examples/tutorial/retry.pdl` shows (`  in text[0]`). What stays 2 -- the notice says what happened and what PDL is doing about it, in PDL's vocabulary, without naming the construct. Why stays 2 -- the exception type and message are shown, formatted, with the attempt counter, but there is no excerpt; the same 2 was already scored on the legible part of the old output under the rubric's "score what the user sees" convention, so the number is unmoved and the wall of text behind it is gone. Fix stays 0: there is nothing for the user to fix, which is the point of the entry.

Shape of the reproducer, unchanged: **a retry that succeeds on the second attempt**, because it is the sharper story -- from the user's point of view nothing went wrong at all, so every byte on stderr was noise, and no one reading the old transcript could tell the run was fine without reading to the end. Determinism comes from `PDL_SESSION`, the module-global `types.SimpleNamespace` that `call_python` injects into every `code:` block: a documented, user-facing idiom (`examples/rag/tfidf_rag.pdl` shares a model between blocks with it), so the program reads as a plausible user program rather than a harness trick, and it does not couple the entry to `trace_error_on_retry`, which has its own test. The alternative shape, `retry: 2` with a `fallback:`, was measured rather than reasoned about: it printed the traceback **twice**, because `trial_total = max_retry + 1` makes `retry: N` mean N *retries* / N+1 attempts and the banner fired once per retry taken -- so the leak scaled with the retry count, and a `retry: 5` block that eventually succeeded dumped five tracebacks onto a successful run. That is also why the counter now says `attempt 1 of 2` rather than `1/1`: it counts attempts against `trial_total`, and `retry: -1` (retry indefinitely) has no total to count towards, so it prints `(attempt 1)`.

Historical: the header read `prog.pdl:0` until phase-3 item 0, when a top-level block's empty path fell through `get_line` to a literal 0 (DROP #4). The normalizer note that every traceback frame here named a real path, and so was rewritten to `line <LINE>`, no longer applies to anything in the golden. INVENTORY's E-RUNTIME-011 row is `[src]` and describes only the *retry exhausted* shape, with location `file:line`; observed, the banner fired on retries taken, not on exhaustion, where the exception is simply re-raised as a normal PDL error. `hygiene_silent_failure` is deliberately **not** set -- this entry was the opposite of silence.
